extracted.intended_audience: mathematics workshop organizers and AIM staff
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for planning and running in-person AIM research workshops, covering daily/weekly schedules, talk format, afternoon group activities, topic selection, facility needs, and logistics/administrative support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily schedule: two morning talks with long break and 2-hour lunch
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two talks each day: both are in the morning, with a long break in between. The lunch break is for 2 hours, beginning whenever the second talk ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talks are scheduled both in the morning (two per day), with a long mid-morning break and a two-hour lunch that starts when the second talk finishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation style: informal, interactive, introductory
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentations are intended to be informal, with lots of questions and answers during the talks. The talks tend to be introductory, serving as preparation for the afternoon activities; they usually are not about "my latest big theorem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage informal delivery and audience interaction; focus on exposition and preparation for collaborative afternoon work rather than presenting personal cutting-edge results.

rubrics_metrics.name: No afternoon talks; afternoons for organized group activities
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no talks in the afternoon. The afternoons are devoted to organized group activities. This could involve a large group discussion or breaking into smaller discussion groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve afternoons exclusively for collaborative sessions (large or small group), problem lists, detailed proof discussions, 'ask the expert' sessions, or beginning longer-term problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-group work: break into groups of 4–6 with daily reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The participants typically break into groups of 4 to 6 people to work on specific topics of interest. Each group gives a brief report to the entire workshop at the beginning of the next afternoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form small groups for focused work; groups may repeat topics across the week or meet only once; incorporate short plenary reports the next day to share progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group topics: examples and repetition allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Example topics include: understanding the details of a difficult proof or construction, discussing possible approaches to a problem, an 'ask the expert' session, or beginning work on a problem which will continue long after the workshop ends. Some group topics are repeated multiple times during the week, while others occur only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow a mix of ephemeral and recurring group topics to match participant interests and to support both immediate learning and ongoing problem development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for selecting topics: coordinated to minimize overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIM staff work with the organizers to determine an appropriate mechanism for selecting topics so that everyone has a group which interests them, but with a minimum of overlap so that people don't miss out on a topic of particular interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either organizers prepare a list of topics in advance or the whole group selects topics via discussion; staff help coordinate to balance interests and avoid duplicative groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly schedule and social events: Monday–Friday 9–5, reception and happy hour
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops run Monday-Friday, 9:00am to 5:00pm each day, with a 2-hour lunch break. Tuesday evening there is a reception and at 5:00 every day we have 'happy hour.' Workshop participants are welcome to arrive as early or stay as late as they wish. There are no afternoons off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate a consistent weekday schedule with built-in social time (reception, daily happy hour); clarify that afternoons are program time and participants should plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning timeline: minimal advance scheduling, fluid day-to-day decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first 5 or 6 talks are determined in advance, and that decision is made about a month before the workshop. No other scheduling decisions are made prior to the workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace fluid scheduling: afternoon activities and later speakers are decided during the workshop (late morning or during lunch), speakers for later days decided one or two days in advance, and each day's schedule is announced the previous afternoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility requirements and amenities
rubrics_metrics.description: A large meeting room has tables, chairs, whiteboards, and a projection system. An adjacent lounge area has high-top tables, couches, and additional whiteboard space. There are five small breakout rooms with ample whiteboards, ceiling projectors, and meeting owls for virtual collaboration. Throughout, moveable partitions allow for flexible use and additional collaboration space. A kitchen area is stocked with coffee, tea, and light refreshments throughout the day, and a social area with couches and games. The eduroam network is available along with AIM-provided wifi throughout the facility. There are four single-occupancy restrooms, including two all-gender restrooms and two with changing tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple collaboration spaces (large room, lounge, breakout rooms) equipped with whiteboards and projection; ensure robust wifi and basic refreshments; make facilities inclusive (all-gender restrooms, changing tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics and organizer support: AIM staff partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIM staff works with the organizers on all aspects of the workshop planning and preparation. This includes the development of the participant list, preparation of lead-in material, and the planning the workshop activities. The administrative logistics, such as sending invitations, keeping track of who has accepted or declined, etc, is handled by the AIM staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect close collaboration with AIM staff, especially since many organizers are inexperienced with the fluid scheduling style; staff handle administrative tasks and assist before and during the workshop.
